sections.heading: Appendix C Algorithm
sections.text: Given a target circle configuration, we translate it into disjunctive normal form f_{1}\lor\dots\lor f_{m}. Each f_{i} is a conjunctive form of circle relations. For each f_{i}, we search a looped chain of circles (in the chain, either a circle or its complement circle can appear, but not both), and let the SphNN determine whether this loop configuration of circles is satisfiable. If one f_{i} is satisfiable, our SphNN will conclude f_{1}\lor\dots\lor f_{m} satisfiable. For example, the configuration \mathbf{P}(\bigcirc_{A},\overline{\bigcirc_{B}}), \mathbf{P}(\overline{\bigcirc_{B}},\bigcirc_{C}), and \neg\mathbf{D}(\bigcirc_{A},\bigcirc_{C}) is a relation among Circle A, the complement of Circle B, and Circle C. Algorithm 1 The main procedure of our SphNN Input: A target circle configuration on an n-dimensional sphere. Output: The input configuration is \mathbf{Satisfiable} or \mathbf{Unsatisfiable} 1 Transform the input configuration into the disjunctive normal form f_{1}\lor\dots\lor f_{m}; 2 Loss \leftarrow+\infty; 3 foreach f_{i}\in[f_{1}\dots f_{m}] do 4 CircleLoop \mbox{get a loop of circles from }f_{i}; 5 if CircleLoop ==\emptyset then 6 \mathbf{continue} 7 else 8 Loss \leftarrow\mbox{construct a configuration for {{CircleLoop}} }; 9 if Loss ==0 then 10 \mathbf{break} 11 if \textnormal{{Loss}}==0 then 12 return \mathbf{Satisfiable} 13 else 14 return \mathbf{Unsatisfiable}
